name: Harsh Mentor
oracle_text: Whenever an opponent activates an ability of an artifact, creature, or land on the battlefield, if it isn't a mana ability, this creature deals 2 damage to that player.
blocked_sentences: Whenever an opponent activates an ability of an artifact, creature, or land on the battlefield, if it isn't a mana ability, this creature deals 2 damage to that player.

needs.what: A DSL trigger event -- `ability_activated` -- that fires when a player activates an activated ability of a permanent, so a card can hang a triggered ability off somebody else's activation. Three pieces: (1) an entry in `TRIGGER_EVENTS` mapping the DSL name to the already-defined `EventType.ABILITY_ACTIVATED`; (2) `game.py:_activate` must use `triggers.fire` instead of `state.emit` at the ABILITY_ACTIVATED emission (line ~488), because `emit` only appends to the log and never calls `collect`, so nothing can ever hear the event as it stands; (3) the event's source permanent must become the trigger's `subject`, i.e. the new name added to `OBJECT_SUBJECT_TRIGGERS` with `_subject_oid` reading the activating permanent's oid off the payload (the emission already passes `source=oid`), so that `TriggerSpec.filter` can express "of an artifact, creature, or land on the battlefield" via the existing `matches_card_filter` types check. `TriggerSpec.controller: "opponent"` then covers "an opponent activates", and `_actor` must return `event.player` (the activating player) for this event rather than the subject's controller, since the subject is the opponent's own permanent in the common case but need not be -- an opponent activating an equip on a creature they do not control must still trigger.
needs.why_existing_wont_do: `trigger_events` in the packet lists 29 DSL events and none is about ability activation. `spell_cast` is the closest -- it is also "an opponent did a thing that used the stack" and already supports `controller: "opponent"` -- but it fires on `EventType.SPELL_CAST` from casting a card off the stack, which is a disjoint set of actions from activating an ability of a permanent already on the battlefield; a Harsh Mentor built on `spell_cast` would punish every instant and sorcery and never punish an equip or a fetchland. `becomes_target` is the other near miss and answers a different question -- it fires on the object being pointed at, so it cannot see an ability with no targets (crack a Signet, sac an Evolving Wilds) and would misfire on every targeted spell. `EventType.ABILITY_ACTIVATED` does exist in `engine/events.py` and is emitted in both activation paths, but via `state.emit`, whose own docstring says it "only records" and leaves the trigger bus to the caller -- so today it is a log line with no listener, and there is no DSL name that could subscribe to it even if there were.
needs.why_it_cannot_be_approximated: There is no other event in the vocabulary that any activation fires. Substituting `spell_cast` or `dealt_damage` would make a card that punishes the wrong actions entirely, and omitting the trigger leaves an inert 2/2 whose only printed line does nothing.

needs.what: A way for an `ability_activated` trigger to exclude mana abilities -- the printed "if it isn't a mana ability" clause. Concretely: put the activated ability's mana-ability status on the ABILITY_ACTIVATED payload (the engine already knows it -- `Ability.is_mana_ability`, read at `legality.py:_is_mana_ability` and `costs.offerable_mana_ability`) and give the trigger spec a boolean restriction on it, e.g. `TriggerSpec.mana_ability: false`, checked in `_matches` beside the existing `not_cause` and `counter` restrictions. Note that the second emission site, `game.py:_activate_mana` (line ~704), emits the identical event type for mana abilities and deliberately bypasses the stack, so it must either keep emitting without firing or fire with the flag set -- but the two paths must stop being indistinguishable to a listener.
needs.why_existing_wont_do: The intervening-if is `condition`, drawn from `condition_keys` (all, any, cast_from_graveyard, cmp, combat_damage_by, evoked, exists, has_city_s_blessing, has_flag, is_your_turn, kicked, left, not, overloaded, right, zone_is), and every one of those asks about the board or about the trigger's own card -- none can ask a property of the ability that fired. `TriggerSpec.filter` runs through `matches_card_filter` against the *source permanent*, so it can say "an artifact, creature, or land" but has no reach into which of that permanent's abilities was used; filtering the permanent's types cannot substitute, because the very permanents this clause is about -- lands and mana artifacts -- are also the permanents whose non-mana abilities Harsh Mentor is printed to punish (a fetchland's sacrifice ability, a Signet's tap-for-mana: same object, opposite answers). Approximating by dropping the clause turns a 2/2 that taxes activated abilities into a Manabarbs that pings every land tap, which is a strictly harsher and different card.
needs.why_it_cannot_be_approximated: Every land in a normal game taps for mana many times per turn; a version without the exclusion would deal double-digit damage in the sandbox position alone and misrepresent the card completely.

notes: Only the trigger side blocks this card; the effect side needs nothing new. Once the event fires, the body is a single `damage` op with `amount: {"const": 2}` and `player: {"binding": "event_player"}` -- `event_bindings` already seeds `event_player` from `event.player` on every trigger, and `select_players` already accepts `{"binding": ...}`, so "that player" is expressible today and is correct in multiplayer rather than collapsing to "opponent". The starting_point (2/2 Human Cleric, {1}{R}, mono-red) needs no change. Sandbox note for whoever closes this: `_activate` is never reached in the expectation harness -- the harness casts the card and stops, so nothing activates an ability -- meaning the eventual answer's expectation is `{"zone": "battlefield"}` plus `battlefield_count: 33`, and the trigger itself must be covered by an engine unit test rather than by the card's expectation.
